Hi, I'm trying to answer bellow

On 06/29/2017 01:25 AM, Mike wrote:

Also I got negative DIC in all the gaussian models, can this be possible?

Yes for continuous likelihood as it is due to density bigger than 1. Example: with small Gaussian likelihood variance. See https://www.mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk/software/bugs/the-bugs-project-dic/#q7

Am I doing right?

Your purpose is to a) fit the data or b) to predict out of the sample? When a) is the case DIC or WAIC will helps. When b) is the case CPO and the RMSE (or something like that) will helps.

Which family better suit my data?

It may depends on the previous point.

Is it more helpful an output for a single model with inla(…verbose=true..)?

I think that plots of the posted results will be helpful. Something like mesh dimension versus one of the measures you want to look at.

Elias

Dear Elias,

Many thanks for your email.

I'm interested in predictions out-of-sample, so I'm going to focus on B option.

I think here the steps I have to follow:

1) run the model using training and validation sets
2) as I get failures (cpo$failure), run manual cpo (inla.cpo()).
3) get the sum of the log CPO from each model with:
slcpo <- function(m, na.rm=TRUE) 
  -sum(log(m$cpo$cpo), na.rm=na.rm)
5) Furthermore, help me with RMSE to evaluate competing model.
6) plot domain inner area triangle resolution as x vs CPO (as I change also outer area triangle resolution, I have several measurements for the same inner resolution), like attached graphs.

Does larger values of slcpo function denote a better fitting?
Does RMSE lower values suggest better fitting?
Both graphs suggest me that 1.2 km inner resolution is my best option because it has the lower RMSE and the higher CPO log sum?
Is variation of CPO and RMSE at 1.2 km inner resolution relevant for my decision? 

Looks decreasing inner triangle resolution improves predictions, with lower CPO and RSME variation, right?

I'll do this for every covariate combination and for each family, then compare which family provide improved predictions, am I right?
Graph are actually done with CPO and RMSE values in posted files. Do I need to recalculate CPO, right?

Many thanks for your help.

Miguel
